title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a coordinated attempt to manipulate AI systems through synthetic content at scale. A fake think tank published over half a million words in nine days designed to appear as neutral research to chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude, presenting one government's positions on contested topics as factual analysis. The failure occurred in the training data and retrieval processes that these systems depend on: they ingested material designed specifically to game their citation preferences without human review to verify the source's authenticity or the claims' accuracy.

The operation exploited a gap between how AI systems find and weight information and how humans typically verify sources. No mechanism caught that the Hanover Institute for Public Policy did not exist, or that the content was produced under foreign government direction rather than emerging from independent research. It would have required either the chatbot platforms to verify source authenticity before indexing, or human reviewers to flag the source during deployment, or both.

It is not established whether the campaign actually influenced the chatbots' outputs, or whether it represents a successful attack on these systems or merely an attempt. The polling data suggesting the broader campaign failed to shift public opinion does not determine whether the AI-focused portion succeeded at a technical level.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
A fake American think tank funded by Israel published over half a million words in nine days to influence artificial intelligence chatbots into making pro-Israel arguments. The website, registered under the nonexistent Hanover Institute for Public Policy, produced 124 reports presenting Israel's positions on topics including Palestinian prisoner torture, war crimes allegations, and Gaza starvation claims as neutral research. The operation used a platform designed to optimize content for citation by major chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude. The New York production company Piro Inc filed the site with the US Justice Department under foreign agent registration requirements.

The broader campaign involves tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government routed through European advertising firm Havas Media to multiple American contractors. Israeli officials have expressed doubts about the strategy's effectiveness, with some comparing it to major past failures. Recent polling shows American support for Israel has declined significantly, with only 36 percent sympathizing with Israel compared to Palestinians, suggesting the messaging operation has failed to shift public opinion despite substantial spending.
